title: Clean Up with a Loop
description: Write cleanup.sh to move every *.tmp file from a spool directory into its archive subdirectory.
scenario: A monitoring agent dumps .tmp files into /home/intern/spool all day and nobody archives them. Your job: write /home/intern/cleanup.sh that moves every *.tmp file from the spool into /home/intern/spool /archive/ using a for loop (no manual one-by-one moves), make it executable and run it once. The non-tmp files must stay where they are.
symptoms: The archive/ subdirectory exists but is empty
keepme.txt and the agent's README must not be touched
The team wants a reusable script, not a one-off command
mission: Create executable /home/intern/cleanup.sh that uses a for loop to move every spool/*.tmp file into spool/archive/, then run it so the spool root is left with zero .tmp files.

hints.title: Glob the pattern
hints.content: `for f in /home/intern/spool/*.tmp` expands the wildcard into one loop iteration per match.

hints.title: Move inside the loop
hints.content: The loop body is just `mv "$f" /home/intern/spool/archive/` — quote the variable so filenames with spaces stay intact.

hints.title: Guard the empty case
hints.content: If no files match, the loop would try to move the literal '*.tmp'. Guard with `[ -e "$f" ] || continue` — good habit for idempotent scripts.

hints.title: Run it
hints.content: `chmod +x cleanup.sh` then `./cleanup.sh` from your home directory.

acceptance_criteria.description: the script uses a for loop
no .tmp files remain in the spool root
all 6 .tmp files are now in spool/archive/
